A22 Settings and integrationsConfigurable values, permissions, keys, and integration status.

Page elements

  • Integration status bar above all tabs: Moyasar, Odoo, OneSignal, OpenLoyalty, PostHog, Adjust, Google Maps (usage percentage of the cap), call center; each badge opens the Integrations tab
  • Tabs: fees, grace periods, dispatch, batching, home, roles, kill switches, integrations, security, quality and trust, languages, calculation basis
  • Settings log (ADM-034): for each value: name, type (percentage, amount, duration, count, list), unit, allowed range, global value and the selected tier's value side by side, version, effective date, scheduled version if any, last editor
  • Level selector: global → region → city, and "a specific store" where the setting supports it (ADM-034); the inherited value is gray "Inherits global/region" and a specific one has a "Specific" badge
  • Currency and time: SAR next to every amount, and the city's time zone next to every effective date (SYS-012)
  • Setting edit panel: the global value for reading, the source of the current value, the allowed range, the new value, "Effective immediately / on a date", the reason, and below it the setting versions (scheduled, in effect, and previous)
  • Approved rules (ADM-034): locked "Approved rule · read-only within the contract" with no edit button
  • Dispatch: the twelve settings of the dispatch algorithm (DSP-001) with their global values and a city-exception column
  • Roles: a list of roles with the number of employees in each (the six ready-made roles and a custom role); a permission × role matrix with values execute/view/no access, highlighting the column of the role being edited and the edited cell in a different color until saved; and the role editor: name, city scope, amount limit for financial actions, permissions
  • Security: two-step verification for read-only access without a kill switch, and the idle time before the session expires (ADM-001)
  • Feature toggles: a feature × city table with its stages (SYS-006), the pilot merchant and driver group for the city (SYS-019), and the minimum allowed version for each app and platform
  • Quality and trust: the "Quality" badge thresholds (MKT-014), the customer refund-rate threshold and what happens when it recurs (SUP-007), no automatic refund (SUP-004), and the Mart damage report window (SUP-009)
  • Languages: data rows (SYS-013), each text with its key and translations, and the number of missing texts per language; notification templates are in A17
  • Calculation basis (read-only): a table of base, tax and invoice for each amount type, and rounding rules (PAY-029)
  • Integrations: for each integration: status, environment (test/live for Moyasar), last successful operation, number of errors today, a test button; for Google Maps: the two caps and the cost so far (SYS-021); for PostHog and Adjust: the list of events sent (INT-008); and MCP: read-only by default
  • Call center: a "Later · not linked" card in integrations (INT-013)

Actions and what happens on each

ActionWhat happens
EditOpens the edit panel at the selected level. "Immediately" creates a version effective now, and "On a date" a scheduled version with a "Scheduled" badge (ADM-034). A notification appears "Version [number] scheduled to take effect [date]"
Connection testSends a check request and shows the result within seconds: "Working · response time" or "Failed" with the provider's message, and updates the status badge; it creates no financial transaction and no notification to a customer
PermissionChecking or removing a permission for a role shows an "Unsaved change" bar with the effect in numbers, "Takes effect immediately for [N] employees". "Save and apply now" applies it at once in the interface and the server (ADM-001), so the buttons disappear in open sessions
Financial limitSets a maximum amount for a role per financial action (refund, compensation, penalty) (ADM-043); the limit is shown read-only in A18 and in the decision window for the role's employee
View logOpens the audit log (A26) filtered by the current tab, setting or role
Cancel scheduled versionAfter confirmation, it deletes the scheduled version before it takes effect, and the current one remains; and the cancellation is logged
Revert to a previous versionCreates a new version with the previous value without erasing history, immediately or on a date
Remove city exceptionA confirmation stating the value the city will inherit; then the region or the global default is inherited from the chosen effective date
Create custom roleEmpty role editor: the name, city scope, permissions from the matrix, the financial limit; "Create role" adds it to the list and it becomes available when assigning employees in A20
Copy roleCreates a custom role with the current role's permissions for editing, named "Copy of ..."
Delete custom roleFor a role with no employees only; otherwise "Move the role's employees first ([count])"
Change feature flag stageMoves a feature in a city between stages after a confirmation stating who will be affected; with no new release (SYS-006)
Edit minimum allowed versionSets the minimum version for each app and platform; older versions ask for an update on open
Add languageAdded as a row, and its missing translation texts appear; it is not enabled until the admin chooses "Enable language"
Switch Moyasar environmentBetween trial and live after a written confirmation, and it is recorded in the audit log

Special states for this page

  • Scheduled version: a "Scheduled" badge and its effective date, then "In effect" automatically at its time
  • Inherited value: shown with its source; editing it creates an exception for the selected level
  • Integration stopped: a red badge and the last success, and text beside it that a stop of PostHog, Adjust, OpenLoyalty, or Odoo does not stop orders or payment
  • Maps cap reached: "Saved estimates are used" badge (SYS-021)
  • Call center not linked: masked call buttons are hidden (INT-013)
  • Unsaved permission change: an alert bar, and leaving the tab asks "Save or discard"
  • Language with incomplete translation: the number of missing texts is shown beside it and it is not activated

Validation and error messages

  • The value has the correct type and unit and is within the allowed range, such as "Starting range does not exceed the maximum range ([value])"
  • Priority-point weights total 100: "Total [N]; must be 100"
  • The effective date is not in the past: "Choose a time after now"
  • The reason is mandatory for every edit: "Enter the reason for the edit"
  • The role name is not duplicated, and a custom role contains at least one permission
  • A change that leaves the system without an employee holding "Roles and permissions" is not saved
  • The minimum allowed version is no lower than the minimum supported version (SYS-006)

Permissions

  • The page is for admin only (Settings, cities, and fees; Roles, permissions, and audit log); the other roles do not see it, and finance sees the financial limits read-only in A18

A26 Audit log NewA single non-deletable log of every financial change or change to roles, permissions, or settings, with who made it, when, and the values before and after.

Page elements

  • Period: shortcuts and custom in Riyadh time
  • Event type: financial, roles and permissions, settings, payouts, the smart assistant (MCP)
  • Executor and executor role: two filters
  • Search: by order number, entry, account, or employee
  • Summary: today's events by type, and the number of rejected attempts
  • Table: time, the executor and their role, the action and entity, before → after in one short column, the source as a badge (dashboard or MCP)
  • Event details in a side panel: before and after side by side, the executor, the time to the second, the scope (cities), the effect, the reason, the reference, and the second approver if any
  • Rejected attempts: what the system rejected (a payout creator trying to approve, an MCP request outside permission, a disallowed city)
  • Permanent alert: the log cannot be deleted or edited from the interface

Actions and what happens on each

ActionWhat happens
FilterFilters and segments update the table and summary instantly, and are saved in the link for sharing with an authorized staff member
Open eventTapping a row shows its details in the side panel without leaving the page
Open entityGoes to the related order, entry, role or setting (A03, A18, A22)
Filter by outletShows all of the same employee's events in the period
ExportExports the filtered results to Excel or PDF; the export itself is recorded as an event

Special states for this page

  • No results for the filter: "No events with these conditions" with a clear-filters button
  • Event from MCP: an "MCP" badge and the original request text, and the financial change appears with the employee's approval inside the dashboard
  • Event with two-person approval (such as a wallet freeze): the requester and the approver and the time of each
  • Rejected event: a row in light red and the reason for rejection

Validation and error messages

  • Period: the start cannot be after the end "Start date is after the end"

Permissions

  • Admin sees all events
  • Finance sees financial events only, from the "Closing and controls" tab in A18
  • No one deletes or edits an event, and there is no button for it (ADM-002)

UX decisions

  • Searching by order number or entry shortens tracing from complaint to decision

22Metric definitions

A unified definition for every number in the dashboards and reports.

One definition for each number is used across all pages and reports, so the same number appears with the same value wherever it is shown (ADM-030, ADM-006). The period is in Riyadh time (REP-001), and the order is attributed to its closing date. Amounts come from the ledger, not from the customer interface.

These definitions are proposed to standardize the calculation, and the owner approves or edits them.

ORD-001 Order statuses Launch-critical
Rules

  • Customer states: Looking for a driver, being prepared, out for delivery, delivered; it stays at being prepared until the driver picks it up.

ORD-003 Order submission and preparation Launch-critical
Rules
  • In menu, Mart, and write-in orders, the driver accepts first, then the order reaches the merchant.
  • The order's default duration is the longest preparation time among the products; write-in takes the store's default duration.
  • The merchant can edit the duration once within 3 minutes of the order arriving; after that the default applies, and the limit is 40 minutes.
  • Preparation starts when the merchant opens the order in the app or 3 minutes after it arrives, whichever comes first, and the preparation time is counted from it (ORD-007).
  • The Ready button is an explicit decision; the invoice is optional in menu and Mart and mandatory in write-in.
  • "Open order" means the merchant opens the order details. The only duration edit allows increasing or decreasing within the 40-minute limit.
  • Mart is like the restaurant: its default duration is adopted automatically, and it has one optional adjustment.
Acceptance criteria
  • Products of 10, 20 and 30 minutes give 30 minutes.
  • Ready works without an invoice in a menu order.
  • Opening the order in the first minute starts preparation immediately.
Pages that use it

M01 Orders · M02 Order details

ORD-004 Cancellation and alternative pickup Launch-critical
Rules
  • The customer can do the usual cancellation within 60 seconds (ORD-002).
  • After the window the order can be cancelled only through the support agent: the support agent refunds the amount to the customer, decides whether there is a penalty and who bears it (the merchant or the driver), and writes the reason (PAY-025).
  • If the driver already picked up the order from the store, the support agent also decides what is paid to the driver and what each party bears.
  • Only two automatic cancellations: an out-of-stock item for which the customer chose "Cancel the order" in advance (MER-032), and a write-in order not paid within 10 minutes (ORD-013). After them the order is referred to support to determine the penalty or the amount charged.
  • No cancellation by the merchant on menu and Mart; they reject write-in only before uploading its invoice, and the order is referred to support.
  • At 5 minutes with no driver, an alert reaches support; at 15 minutes support intervenes and offers a non-Mart customer self-pickup within 5 minutes or a full refund.
  • Mart has no self-pickup; after 15 minutes support handles assignment or cancellation and refund, without moving to another grocery.
  • If the customer does not choose something other than Mart within 5 minutes, the order is cancelled and the amount is refunded in full automatically, and an alert reaches support.
  • The bearer in the cancellation dialog: the merchant, the driver, the platform, or "No penalty."
Acceptance criteria
  • No reject button on a menu or Mart order.
  • No self-pickup option for Mart.
  • The system does not deduct a penalty merely for cancellation.
  • A cancellation after the timeout is not saved without an actor and a written reason, and without specifying the bearing party or "No penalty".
Pages that use it

ORD-009 Location correction Important
Rules
  • The customer corrects their location even after the driver receives the order.
  • If the new location is farther, the system adds the fee and sends a payment request to the customer.
  • If the new location is outside the zone, a direct alarm reaches support to resolve the problem.
  • If the customer refuses to pay the difference, an alert reaches the operations room and the driver. The driver continues to the first location with no extra fee, and the order is not cancelled. The refusal is recorded on the order, and no penalty is imposed on the customer
  • The window to pay the location-correction difference is 3 minutes, and its expiry counts as a rejection.
Acceptance criteria
  • The location does not change until the customer pays the difference.
  • If the location is outside the zone, it creates an alarm for support.
  • If the customer refuses to pay the difference, the order is not cancelled, and the driver continues to the first location.

ORD-013 Write-in orders Launch-critical
Rules

Payment, fees, and adjustments PAY27

PAY-001 Payment and hold Launch-critical
Rules
  • Online payment via Moyasar
  • The amount stays held on the customer's payment method until the order is closed, then the system captures what is due and cancels the hold on the rest.
  • The order is closed in one of these cases: delivery, or ending the order due to no response (ORD-008), or returning the medicine to the pharmacy (PHR-010), or a support decision on a cancellation or a "not received" case. In a support decision, only what support specified is captured.
  • The system releases the hold in full if the customer cancels within the grace period or no driver was found and the customer chose the refund.
  • Payment methods available are Mada, Visa, Mastercard, Apple Pay, and STC Pay according to what Moyasar supports, and all support the hold.
  • The administrator disables any payment method from settings without an app update.
Acceptance criteria
  • The system does not capture the amount before the order is closed in one of the listed statuses.
  • If a payment notification repeats, the system does not repeat the deduction.
Pages that use it

C09 Cart and checkout · C10 My orders · C11 Order tracking · C12 Out-of-stock item and substitute · C24 No driver or coverage

PAY-002 Wallet and rewards Launch-critical
Rules
  • Credit has three types: refund (does not expire), compensation (14 days), and promotional (14 days).
  • Promotional credit comes from invite a friend, the loyalty program, gifts and cashback. For each promotional credit it is set who funds it: the platform or the merchant
  • The customer does not top up their wallet or withdraw from it.
  • Any compensation reaches the customer as a reward with a notification. The customer taps the notification and the reward page opens with a "Claim reward" button. When tapped, the amount reaches their wallet immediately
  • The reward lapses if it is not claimed within 24 hours of the notification arriving.
  • The system spends the credit that expires first before others, and spends refund credit last.
  • The wallet shows each balance with its type and expiry date.
  • Wallet balance is allowed in both write-in order payments: delivery and the invoice.
  • Promotional credit funded by a merchant is deducted from them only when actually used in an order from their store; if it expires unused, the merchant pays nothing.
  • Balances migrated from the current app become refund credit (SYS-020).
Acceptance criteria
  • The system does not spend a promotional credit that is 15 days old.
  • Spending starts with the nearest to expiry
  • A reward not claimed within 24 hours lapses.
Pages that use it

  • If the customer chooses to convert a card refund to the wallet, it becomes permanent refund credit and is added immediately; there is no reward claim window.
  • Excess compensation alone is a reward with a 24-hour claim window.

PAY-004 Price and fee rule Launch-critical
Rules
  • The customer's menu price is the selling price entered by the manager (MER-002).
  • Mart: merchant price × (1 + customer price increase), default 5%.
  • The restaurant percentage is on the selling price minus the discount borne by the merchant; a platform discount does not reduce the merchant commission base.
  • The customer service fee is calculated per PAY-021.
  • The wallet is a payment method and does not reduce the fee base; the contract copy and settings are saved on the order.
Acceptance criteria
  • The wallet does not charge twice.
  • A service fee is not charged on itself or on a tip.

PAY-005 Financial ledger Launch-critical
Rules
  • The double-entry ledger is the single reference for money, and is built before any financial screen
  • Every movement is recorded as a balanced two-sided entry. An entry is not edited; it is corrected by a reversing entry
  • A chart of accounts and a journal entry template are written for each financial event before coding. An explicit ruling is also written for each forfeiture case: a reward not claimed, expired cashback, and promotional credit funded by a merchant
  • The system checks daily that the sum of entries is zero
  • Odoo receives what the system exports from the ledger
  • Forfeiture rule: what the platform funded (a reward not claimed within 24 hours, expired promotional credit, expired points) returns to it as revenue under the name "Forfeited amounts".
Acceptance criteria
  • An admin dashboard user cannot adjust any party's balance directly
  • The total of any day's entries is zero
  • When a reward lapses, an entry is recorded for it specifying its destination
Pages that use it

PAY-006 Settlements and payouts Launch-critical
Rules
  • The system shows a real-time statement for each merchant, freelance driver and company
  • Payouts are made through Moyasar's payment distribution service, because the platform holds the merchants' and drivers' funds
  • At the payout date (weekly for merchants, and on its date for drivers and companies) the system prepares the dues list, and no payout is sent without manual approval.
  • Whoever holds the "Approve payouts" permission approves after reviewing the account statement: a single account, or selects several accounts and approves them together.
  • Delivery companies' dues are paid to the company only
  • Each payout appears with its status, its bank reference, and its date. Statuses: in progress, sent, or failed
  • Freelance driver payouts are weekly on the same payout day as merchants, by manual approval.
  • A merchant whose new bank account is awaiting finance approval does not enter the payout list (MER-001).
Acceptance criteria
  • A failed payout does not appear as paid
  • A payout is not sent without an approval recorded with the approver's name and time.
  • Selecting 10 accounts and approving sends 10 payouts and records an approval for each account.
  • The statement shows all deductions, compensation and offers

  • Shows the customer the purchase order: products, delivery, service, tip, discounts and payment source.
  • Uploaded invoices are saved linked to the order; the absence of the optional invoice does not block Ready or delivery.
  • The merchant's monthly platform fee statement and invoice linked to orders, and a refund is corrected with a reversal entry and a linked notification.

  • Write-in does not bypass the invoice requirement.

PAY-009 Restaurant and Shops contracts Launch-critical
Rules
  • The two contract types: a fee per new customer in each branch (PAY-010), or a percentage the manager agrees with the merchant.
  • The contract percentage is always calculated on the selling price minus the merchant's share of the discount only.
  • From an exempt menu link, the contract percentage or per-customer contract fee is not deducted; the payment fee and the customer service fee remain.
  • These two contracts are for restaurants and Shops with a menu; Mart and pharmacies use their percentages (PAY-012).
Acceptance criteria
  • The contract type is one of percentage or a fee per customer and branch.
  • An item with a selling price of 110 and a contract percentage of 10%: the platform deducts 11.
  • Fee contract: no percentage is deducted from the merchant; only the customer fee is deducted (PAY-010).

A06 Merchant page

PAY-010 Contract fees per customer and branch — deducted from the merchant Launch-critical
Rules
  • This is a fee on the merchant according to their contract type, independent of the customer service fee shown in the payment summary.
  • The due is 2 SAR for an order whose selling prices total less than 25, and 5 SAR from 25 and above.
  • Each customer and branch has an independent 365-day cycle from the first order; the cycle cap is 30 SAR.
  • Actual = min(due, max(0, 30 − cycle total)).
  • A new cycle starts at the first order after 365 days have passed, not with an automatic daily reset without a request.
  • The fee is fixed at capture with the counter locked; a refund reverses the actual fee only.
  • An exempt-link order carries no fee and does not increase the counter.
  • The fee is deducted from the merchant on each new-customer order until its total reaches 30 SAR at the branch, then nothing more is deducted until its cycle ends.
Acceptance criteria
  • A total of 26 and 5 due gives 4.
  • At 30 the fee is zero.
  • Two simultaneous orders do not exceed the cap of 30.
  • A new customer at the branch ordered at a selling price of 20 then 40 then 60: 2 then 5 then 5 is deducted.

PAY-011 Online payment fee Launch-critical
Rules
  • Fixed for restaurants and Shops: 2.5% of the product value after discount + 1 SAR; excludes delivery, service fees, and the tip.
  • Stays with the menu link exemption.
  • Mart and pharmacies do not bear this fee; the actual Moyasar fee is recorded as a separate platform expense.
  • The fixed SAR amount is once per order when its products are captured; the payment provider's fees on the two write-in payments are recorded as a separate expense, without repeating the merchant's fixed fee.
Acceptance criteria
  • Products 100 and delivery 20 give a merchant fee of 3.50.
  • Products 105 and discount 20 give a merchant fee of 3.13 (2.5% of 85 + 1).
  • The payment fee does not appear on Mart and pharmacy.

  • The Mart basis is the merchant's original price, not the customer price after the markup.
  • Mart adds a 5% increase (by default) inside the product price for the customer, with the general service fee per PAY-021.
  • The pharmacy shows the original invoice and a 5% service fee on products as a separate line; the merchant percentage applies to the value of the invoice products.

PAY-013 Delivery fees Launch-critical
Rules
  • The delivery fee is a system-wide setting: a base fee covering a set number of kilometers, a price per extra kilometer, and a minimum and a maximum.
  • Distance is measured from the store to the customer by a setting: straight line (default), or a Google Maps route if the call cost is acceptable within the SYS-021 cap; when the cap is reached, the straight line is used.
  • The distance and the method used to measure it are saved on the order when it is confirmed.
  • An optional setting can be added for any city; a city with no setting takes the global setting.
  • There is one fee schedule for restaurants and miscellaneous shops, and another for Mart and pharmacies
  • Pricing rules with scope, priority, and effective date: a specific store, then city, then the global setting.
  • The driver wage has rules independent of the customer price, so delivery offers do not reduce it (PAY-014)
  • Defaults for the general setting: restaurants and various shops 9 SAR including 3 km, and 1.5 SAR per additional kilometer, minimum 9 and maximum 25. Mart and pharmacies 12 SAR including 3 km, and 1.5 SAR per additional kilometer, minimum 12 and maximum 30.
  • A partial extra kilometer is rounded up: 2.3 km counts as 3 km.
Acceptance criteria
  • When a city's fees change, no confirmed order changes
  • If the calculated fees exceed the maximum, the system applies the maximum
  • The system does not apply a rule whose effective date is in the future before that date
  • A city without a specific setting takes the global setting.
  • A restaurant 4.2 km away: 9 SAR for the first three kilometers + 2 × 1.5 = 12 SAR.

  • A delivery company driver is outside this ranking: their dues are calculated for their company at the platform percentage in the company contract (FLT-002).
  • Tip: 15% is deducted and the rest reaches the driver in full with no platform percentage (CUS-010).

  • When the driver is switched, the pay and tip go to whoever delivered; any compensation to the first is a documented manual decision with no automatic deduction.
  • The default platform percentage of driver pay is 10%.

  • A city exception overrides the tier percentage.
  • A company driver does not get tier benefits in the percentage.

PAY-025 Manual penalties Launch-critical
Rules
  • No automatic financial penalties; delay, cancellation, or an alert does not create a deduction entry.
  • A support agent imposes the penalty manually on a merchant or driver after reviewing the evidence, and sets its amount and who bears it.
  • The operation requires a linked order or case, a written reason, an amount, an executor, a date and evidence. If admin sets a limit for the staff role, anything above it needs a second approval (ADM-043).
  • The affected party is notified and the reason appears in their statement, and they can appeal; reversing the decision is by a reversal entry.
  • The outcome of the amount is decided manually: platform, customer compensation, or return; compensation is not a refund of an amount the customer paid.
  • "The platform" is an option for the bearer with a written reason, and is recorded as a platform expense.
  • The outcome "Return" means using the penalty amount to refund what the customer actually paid; and "Compensation" is added as credit to the customer.
  • The deduction remains in effect during the appeal with the status "Under appeal", and is reversed with a reversal entry if the appeal is accepted.
Acceptance criteria
  • No financial movement for merely a 10-minute delay.
  • An employee whose role has no penalties permission does not execute a deduction.
  • The deduction is visible, explained, and traceable.

PAY-026 Negative balance and driver security deposit Launch-critical
Rules
  • Approved manual deductions or charging an actual loss may produce a negative balance in the driver's wallet, and it is deducted from their next payout.
  • If the wallet balance reaches −50 SAR or less (setting), the driver stops receiving new tasks until they pay; there is no automatic suspension because of a delay penalty.
  • A negative balance is not settled from the deposit during work; it is settled from it only when the account is closed, and the deposit is not returned before settlement.
  • The driver pays the negative balance electronically from the app via Moyasar, and returns to receiving tasks as soon as it is paid.
Acceptance criteria
  • A balance of −49 does not stop tasks, and a balance of −50 stops them.
  • An unapproved deduction does not affect the balance.
  • Closing the account does not go beyond settling the balance.

PAY-028 Recalculation and partial refund Launch-critical
Rules
  • A single financial function recalculates the remaining items, the service, the contract, the online payment fee, and tax on the original order copy.
  • Editing before capture (deleting an item or a substitute) reduces only the captured amount, with no reversal entries.
  • Editing after capture refunds only the difference in the fee paid; a capped contract is recalculated using the counter locked at order capture (PAY-010), not a current counter that changed with later orders.
  • A reversal entry for the difference and for each party after capture; the refunded customer fee is returned to the counter of its original cycle and does not reduce the counter of a new cycle.
  • Removed items, cheaper substitutes and returned medicine enter processing; an increase requires customer acceptance and payment of the difference before it is locked in.
  • The fixed part of the payment fee is once per order when there is a product capture; its refund on full cancellation follows the refund decision, while the provider's actual cost remains an expense.
Acceptance criteria
  • Products under 25 give 2 due before the cap limit.
  • The new fee does not increase the contract fee paid in a partial refund.
  • Replaying the event does not repeat the reply.
  • Deleting an item before capture does not create a reversing entry.

  • Points are rounded down
  • Everything the customer pays (products, delivery, and service fee) includes 15% tax: delivery of 12 SAR, of which 10.43 is before tax.

  • The accountant approves the table before coding, then the examples are declared final.

  • Every row in "Financial transaction examples" matches the calculation result to the halala

MER-032 Substitute for an out-of-stock product Launch-critical
Rules
  • At payment the customer chooses in advance what the merchant does if a product is out of stock: remove it, call me, or cancel the order.
  • If the customer chooses "Call me", they specify the number the merchant calls: their registered number or another one.
  • If the merchant taps "Out of stock" on an item and the customer had chosen "Call me", the merchant sees the number the customer chose to call. This is an exception to the customer-data hiding rule, and applies to this order only
  • The 3-minute window starts the moment the merchant presses "Out of stock". After calling, the merchant records the customer's response with one button: "Substitute", "Remove", or "Cancel".
  • If the merchant does not record a response within 3 minutes, the system applies the "Remove it" option.
  • The merchant proposes deletion or a substitute, and the customer agrees and pays the price difference if the substitute costs more
  • If all the order's items are removed, or the customer had chosen "Cancel the order", the system cancels the order automatically and the customer is refunded, and the reason "Item out of stock" is recorded.
  • After this cancellation the order is referred to support, and the support agent decides on a penalty on the merchant for the out-of-stock item if they see fit, writing the reason (PAY-025).
  • The system hides the customer's number from the merchant when the customer replies, or when "Delete it" is applied after the 3-minute grace period ends, or when the order closes.
  • If the customer accepted a more expensive substitute and the difference hold fails, the item is removed and the customer is notified.
  • "Out of stock" is not available after pressing "Ready"; any problem after that is escalated to support.
  • The default option when out of stock is "Delete it", and the customer's last choice is saved.
Acceptance criteria
  • The number does not appear to the merchant until they press "Out of stock" and the customer has chosen "Call me".
  • If no response is recorded within 3 minutes of tapping "Out of stock", the item is removed
  • The "Cancel" button cancels the order as in the automatic cancellation due to out-of-stock.
  • The number does not appear in the order list, in the order details, or in merchant reports. It appears only for the item the merchant pressed "Out of stock" on, in an order where the customer chose "Call me"
  • When the customer replies, the 3-minute timeout ends, or the order is closed, the number no longer appears to the merchant afterward.
  • Automatic cancellation due to out of stock does not create a penalty; the penalty is a manual decision by support.
Pages that use it

  • By default: New for the first 30 orders, Under watch below 70, Silver 70–79, Gold 80–89, Diamond 90 and above.

  • Scores exclude merchant delay, customer cancellation, and technical failure.
  • Admin configures how indicators convert to points; the default is linear from zero to the target, capped at the indicator's weight; an indicator with no data is excluded and the remaining weights are normalized to 100.
  • The first 30 orders are a new tier; no automatic financial penalty from a drop in score.
  • Default targets: completion 98%, on-time delivery 90%, on-time pickup 90%, acceptance 80%, rating 4.8, complaints zero, and compliance 95%.

  • The absence of ratings is not treated as zero satisfaction.

DRV-023 Penalty ladder and appeal Launch-critical
Rules
  • Five consecutive steps apply to the driver: a warning, then lower priority for a week, then a 24-hour suspension, then a review by operations, then a permanent suspension.
  • The system suspends the driver immediately, without gradual steps, in these cases: fraud, location spoofing, account sharing, and abuse of a customer.
  • The system notifies the driver of the reason for each step.
  • The driver appeals within 7 days, and gets the response within 48 hours
  • The ladder steps are carried out manually by an operations employee or a support supervisor after review, not automatically by the system.
  • Violations that move the driver one step: a proven complaint, or 3 apologies after acceptance in one week, or leaving without permission.
  • The driver returns to the start of the ladder after 90 days without a violation.
Acceptance criteria
  • The system does not suspend a driver without the reason being shown to them.
  • 3 post-acceptance declines in a week appear to operations as a violation, and the system does not move the driver a step by itself.

Dispatch and cities DSP5

DSP-001 Dispatching orders to drivers Launch-critical
Rules
  • Filtering: online and active, service and city allowed, not blocked by the store or customer, recent location, suitable equipment, and available capacity.
  • Distribution starts after the customer's 60-second cancellation window ends (ORD-002), and the 15-minute window is counted from it.
  • Each eligible driver has "priority points" out of 100: the driver score (DRV-017, including the rating) 50%, delivery volume in the last 30 days compared to the top driver in the city 30%, and proximity to the store 20%.
  • The preferred captain gets a solo 30-second offer first if the manager has set one; if he does not respond, the order returns to the sequence without changing the 15 timeout.
  • First attempt: 5 km range and top 3 by points. Second: 6 km and top 6. Third: 7 km and all qualified. Each attempt has 30 seconds to accept, with 10 seconds between them.
  • Next rounds: the radius expands 1 km each attempt up to 10 km then holds, and it is offered to all eligible; repeats up to 15 minutes.
  • The first atomic acceptance wins, and the card is withdrawn from the rest. No double assignment.
  • Whoever explicitly declined is not offered the same order again; whoever ignored the offer is offered it in the next round.
  • Distance is a straight line from the driver's current location to the store. A driver with a task enters if the batching conditions are met (DSP-003).
  • A new driver (first 30 orders) has a score of 70 in the calculation. Anyone who stays online for an hour with no order moves up the list for the next order.
  • Support alert at 5 minutes; at 15 support intervenes and the ORD-004 handling is executed.
  • All values are global system settings and can be edited per city; they are not hard-coded constants.
  • If the store has more than one available preferred captain, the order is offered to them together for 30 seconds, and the first to accept takes it, then the order returns to the normal sequence.
Acceptance criteria
  • Proximity points = (1 − distance ÷ attempt range) × 100.
  • Khaled (score 78, 260 deliveries, 1 km) = 85 points; Ahmed (92, 180, 3 km) = 75; Salem the newcomer (70, 12, 0.5 km) = 54; when the top driver has 260 and the range is 5 km.
  • With 5 eligible within 5 km the first attempt is shown only to the top 3 by points.
  • No double assignment.
  • Leaving the area or a ban excludes the task.
  • A city setting overrides the global setting.
Pages that use it

  • The order is assigned manually by driver number, with the reason stated.
  • A manual assignment reaches the driver already assigned directly with the reason, and the driver may decline only with the reasons in ORD-014, and it is recorded in their performance.
Acceptance criteria
  • A customer outside the store's city cannot order from it
  • If the driver has a specific zone, no order outside that zone is offered to them.

MKT-001 Coupons Launch-critical
Rules
  • These properties are set for each coupon: cities, stores, categories, customers, period, usage limit, budget, funding, and stacking.
  • "First order" offers are granted once per mobile number, per device, and per payment method. They are not granted to a device previously used with another account.
  • The offer targets the customer segment relative to the store: new, existing, or dormant (has not ordered from the store for a period the manager sets)
  • The coupon can be limited to the cards of a specific issuing bank, and the bank or the platform then funds it per the agreement.
  • A configurable setting that determines whether the coupon may be combined with wallet credit, which the manager enables or disables
Acceptance criteria
  • A city coupon does not work outside it
  • The last budget is not used twice
  • A new account on a device previously used does not get the "First order" offer.
  • The dormant customers coupon does not work for a customer who ordered from the store within the period.
Pages that use it

A14 Offers and coupons

MKT-002 Consecutive-order rewards Launch-critical
Rules
  • A support agent sets the consecutive-orders reward for the customer manually: the amount and the reason, and it is added as promotional credit (PAY-002).
  • The promotional credit is used across several orders.
Acceptance criteria
  • A canceled order does not consume a reward
  • The reward is not granted without a recorded actor and reason.

MKT-003 Ad placements Launch-critical
Rules

  • Admin sets the price of each placement, its city, duration, and capacity.
  • The merchant sees the price before submitting the campaign, and the amount is deducted from their dues after approval; no publishing and no deduction before approval.
  • Pausing a campaign for platform reasons refunds the unexecuted portion; a pause at the merchant's request applies a placement policy visible before ordering.
  • If the merchant stops an ad at their request, the remaining full days are refunded, and the current day is not refunded.
Acceptance criteria
  • The price appears before the campaign is sent.
  • No keywords field.

  • The merchant does not get customers' numbers; audience counts and results are shown.
  • Repetition limits, budget, and templates come from admin.
  • Campaigns to the store's customers are free at launch and go through admin approval. Segments: new, repeat, and lapsed for 30 days. The limit is one message per week per customer from the same store.

  • The scope excludes the unserved customer.

MKT-007 Offers and funding Launch-critical
Rules
  • The admin deal activates as soon as the eligible merchant subscribes.
  • The merchant's own deal is reviewed before it is published; admin can create it on their behalf.
  • Each offer has a scope, areas, stores, products, duration, stock, minimum, budget, and a stacking rule.
  • Its funding is percentages or amounts per party; the actual cost is split and double charging is prevented.
  • If combining is not allowed, the offer with the highest saving for the customer applies after its conditions are met; the allowed combination follows an order saved on the order.
  • A platform-funded discount does not reduce the merchant's commission; the merchant's discount reduces its base.
  • If a merchant's offer is rejected, they see the reason, edit it and resubmit.
  • Ending a merchant's subscription to an admin offer takes effect immediately on new orders.
Acceptance criteria
  • A deal outside the store's range does not appear.
  • Subscribing to an admin offer does not enter a new review.
  • The funding share must not exceed the offer cost.

MKT-010 Customer loyalty via OpenLoyalty Important
Rules
  • Points and rules are run through OpenLoyalty; the Mahallat ledger is the financial reference, and the integration passes events with unique identifiers.
  • Order points come from the platform net after the offer funder, the coupon and the Moyasar fee; a base ≤ 0 gives no points.
  • Points are pending until the end of the complaint window and are withdrawn on refund.
  • The value, limit, expiry and cap per city or period, and the double points the merchant buys, are settings.
  • Failure of the tool does not stop the order; the event is re-synced without a duplicate reward.
  • Points can be redeemed from 500 points, and expire after 12 months.
  • The points-to-SAR conversion rate is a configurable value set by the manager per city or period, and has no fixed value in the code; the page shows the value in SAR according to the rate in effect.
Acceptance criteria
  • A duplicate event does not duplicate points.
  • The financial liabilities of points appear in SAR.

C06 Pharmacies

EXT-006 Self-pickup Launch-critical
Rules
  • For menu orders other than Mart: the customer orders and pays, and after the 60-second cancellation window (ORD-002) the order reaches the merchant without a driver and delivery.
  • No self-pickup for Mart, nor for write-in and pharmacy orders at launch.
  • Discount and scope per the store's setting and its funder.
  • The Ready page remains with directions, the reminder, and the alert after 60 minutes; without a customer code.
  • The merchant confirms pickup with the order number. If the customer does not collect by the end of business hours, the order is closed "Not collected" and referred to support, and the support agent decides what is captured and what is refunded.
  • After 15 minutes with no driver, conversion is available for 5 minutes; delivery is refunded, and the conversion discount is borne by the platform.
  • No extra deduction when converting to self-pickup at launch: only delivery and tip are refunded; and the conversion deduction is a setting whose default value is zero.
  • Stores in the customer's city within 10 km are shown for self-pickup (a per-store setting). The order is blocked if the expected readiness is after the branch closes.
  • The 60-minute alert is counted from "Ready", and reaches the customer and the merchant.
Acceptance criteria
  • The page is saved without a code.
  • The switch reverses delivery once.
  • A customer cancellation within 60 seconds prevents the order from reaching the merchant.
  • A "not received" order is not captured before the support decision.

C06 Pharmacies · C11 Order tracking

PHR-010 Unresponsiveness in medicine orders Launch-critical
Rules
  • The status of a medicine order that was not delivered is "Returning to the pharmacy", and the driver returns the medicine to the pharmacy
  • The return is done with a code like the pickup code, and the pharmacy enters this code.
  • The reorder window is configurable. After it ends, an alert reaches operations to decide, even if the pharmacy is closed
  • The customer does not get the delivery fee back, and gets back the medicine price and the 5% service fee after the pharmacy confirms the return is safe. Rejecting the refund is an operations decision based on the pharmacy's confirmation, and then the medicine remains the customer's property.
  • The default reorder window is 60 minutes.
  • Re-delivering the medicine to the customer is a new order with a new delivery fee.
  • No extra wage for the driver for the return trip to the pharmacy; they earned their full wage and tip.
Acceptance criteria
  • A medicine order is not closed before the return code is entered or an operations decision is issued.
  • When the timeout ends, an alert reaches operations.
  • Medicine 100 and service 5 returned intact: 105 is refunded to the customer and the delivery fee is not refunded.
Pages that use it

PHR-012 Pharmacy order Launch-critical
Rules
  • The customer writes their order, attaches the prescription if any, then pays for delivery first (ORD-013).
  • Before sending, the customer sees an alert: if the medicine needs a prescription and the customer did not attach one, the order is canceled
  • The pharmacist reviews the order and the prescription, then prepares the order, and attaches the invoice and its amount.
  • 5% is added to the customer, then the customer pays, and after that the driver picks up the order.
  • When a prescription medicine is requested without a prescription, the pharmacist rejects the order before uploading the invoice, and it is referred to support; the support agent decides what portion of the delivery fee is refunded and what is paid to the driver, writing the reason. The customer receives a cancellation message.
  • The driver does not see the prescription
Acceptance criteria
  • A pharmacy order rejected for lack of a prescription is not closed before the support decision on the delivery fee.

  • Saves the view's period and filters; prevents a start after the end, and the screen clarifies whether the end day is included.

  • A range whose start is after its end is not executed.
  • Exporting the period matches the figures on the screen.

Build and operations SYS21

SYS-001 One project with non-overlapping modules Launch-critical
Rules
  • Each module is a folder with a public interface and its own tables, and no module reads another module's tables
  • A checking tool runs on every build and prevents that.
  • A new service (such as Taxi) is a module that uses the dispatch, pricing, payments, and finance modules
Acceptance criteria
  • The build fails if a module reads tables belonging to another module.
SYS-002 Fees, durations and operating limits in settings Launch-critical
Rules
  • Sections, store types, statuses, fees, tiers, incentives, the home page, and roles are stored in admin dashboard tables and settings. This way an authorized administrator edits them without releasing a new version.
  • The code reads the section's property and does not depend on its name.
Acceptance criteria
  • When a new section or a new tier of the supported types is added, it is done from settings without development.
Pages that use it

A22 Settings and integrations

SYS-003 Order, task and trip Launch-critical
Rules
  • The driver task is independent of the order and has pickup, delivery and return stops; the trip groups tasks according to a configurable capacity, default 3.
  • An order has independent payments for each purpose, status, and reference, including the two write-in payments.
  • Contract versions are dated; an important shared foundation that is extensible for deferred taxi.
Acceptance criteria
  • A change in payment status does not falsify delivery.
  • Batching keeps the stop order and each order's time.
SYS-004 Internal events Launch-critical
Rules
  • Every important change triggers an event. The event is written together with the change itself, then distributed in the background
  • Notifications, accounting, and reports listen to these events, and a new feature is added as a new listener
Acceptance criteria
  • If notifications fail, the order does not stop.
SYS-005 Durable scheduler for all timeouts Launch-critical
Rules
  • Timeouts and scheduling are in the database, and resume after a server restart.
  • The server clock is the reference for windows and states; device events are logged evidence.
  • Repeating the scheduler's task does not repeat a cancellation, a refund, a notification, or an entry.
Acceptance criteria
  • A server restart does not lose the expiry time of a write-in invoice.
SYS-006 Feature flags and remote configuration Launch-critical
Rules
  • A toggle for each feature and city; starts closed, then a pilot city, then rollout.
  • The app fetches the minimum allowed version, toggles, translations and the home order from the server.
  • Editing content and settings does not need a store update; app code changes are distributed according to the release mechanism suitable for the platform.
Acceptance criteria
  • Pausing a section in a city does not need a new release.
  • The setting does not go below the minimum supported version.
Pages that use it

A22 Settings and integrations

SYS-007 Server-driven home Launch-critical
Rules
  • The server sends the home page as ordered blocks for each city.
  • The app ignores any block it does not recognize.
Acceptance criteria
  • When a seasonal row is added in settings it appears in the app without a new release.
SYS-008 Versioned APIs Launch-critical
Rules
  • A change within the release is by addition only.
  • Old versions of the apps continue to work.
Acceptance criteria
  • When the server is updated, the old app version does not break.
SYS-009 External services adapter Launch-critical
Rules
  • Moyasar, the cashier, maps, messaging and the call center sit behind separate interfaces and adapters, each with a sandbox substitute that needs no real keys.
  • The reference result used is saved on the order, so switching the provider does not change times or constraints of old orders.
Acceptance criteria
  • Replacing the provider does not change the calculation of a completed order.
SYS-010 Duplicate operation prevention Launch-critical
Rules
  • Every command that creates an order or moves money carries a unique key.
  • On a weak network, the system does not create two orders or move money twice.
Acceptance criteria
  • When the same order is resent, the system does not create a second order.
SYS-011 Reports from a read replica Launch-critical
Rules
  • Reports and the smart assistant read from a separate copy
  • The definition of each indicator is written once.
Acceptance criteria
  • If a heavy report runs at peak time, orders do not slow down.
SYS-012 Regions, currency and time zone Launch-critical
Rules
  • A single table for regions in a hierarchy (country, region, city), and each level inherits settings from the level above it
  • A currency field beside each amount
  • Times are stored in UTC with the city's time zone, and VAT is stored with an effective date
Acceptance criteria
  • A city-specific setting applies to it alone, and the rest of the region's cities inherit the region setting or the global setting.

SYS-013 Translation and notification templates Launch-critical
Rules

  • A new language, such as Urdu, is added as data rows

Pages that use it

A17 Notifications · A22 Settings and integrations

SYS-014 Environments and automated testing Launch-critical
Rules
  • There are three environments: development, staging, and production, each with a separate database and separate keys.
  • There are demo versions of the three apps, a fake city, and a "driver simulator".
  • Every acceptance criterion has an automated test carrying its identifier, and every row in "Financial operation examples" has a test in which amounts are computed in halalas
  • Procedural criteria that are not tested automatically (such as the Moyasar trial before launch in INT-001, and the monthly restore drill in SYS-015) are tracked in a manual acceptance checklist under the same ID, and do not block publishing.
  • Automated tests run with every change, and publishing is blocked if any of them fails.
  • The "financial operations examples" tests are approved after the accountant approves the base and VAT table (PAY-029).
Acceptance criteria
  • A release with a failing automated test is rejected
SYS-015 Monitoring and backup Launch-critical
Rules
  • Availability check every minute. An alert reaches the owner's phone when errors rise, payment fails, Moyasar notifications stop, scheduled tasks pile up, or the message balance runs out
  • A tool that collects errors with the version number, logs that carry the order number, and a "Failed events" list with a retry button
  • Automatic daily backup, with the ability to restore to any moment within 7 days. Backups include images, invoices and prescriptions, and restoration is tested monthly
Acceptance criteria
  • The monthly restore test succeeds and its result is logged.
SYS-016 Secrets and signing keys Launch-critical
Rules
  • Secrets are stored on the server only, and are not placed in the apps or the repository.
  • App signing keys, store accounts, and service passwords are kept in a vault under the company's name
Acceptance criteria
  • The apps' code contains no secret key.
SYS-017 Performance targets Launch-critical
Rules
  • 95% of server requests under 500 milliseconds, and the home page under 2 seconds on an average phone.
  • After the assignment event, the order reaches the merchant's device and the task card reaches the driver within 3 seconds.
  • Location is sent every 20 seconds by default; it is displayed within 10 seconds of receipt, and the last update time is shown.
  • Monthly availability target is 99.5% in the first year; the last location is in a fast cache and bulk messages go in batches.
  • A load test of 400 drivers sending every 5 seconds to test a margin above the operational setting.
Acceptance criteria
  • The load test passes with no lost events or duplicate assignment.
  • An old location of 120 seconds is excluded from a new distribution.
SYS-018 Weak network Launch-critical
Rules
  • The driver's app saves its events with the device time and location and sends them in order when connected.
  • The operational decision time comes from the server; the device time is a hint corrected by the last sync offset, and it does not revive an expired order or cancel a new assignment.
  • The merchant's request via direct connection, notification, and periodic polling, with automatic calling as a fallback.
  • A customer disconnecting after payment does not duplicate the order; no delivery code is stored for the customer.
Acceptance criteria
  • A late event does not reopen a closed task.
  • Retrying the payment does not create two orders.
SYS-019 Gradual rollout Launch-critical
Rules
  • The platform is piloted with a group of merchants and drivers in a single city.
  • Cities and sections are opened with operating switches and the city checklist (ADM-037).
  • App updates are released on the stores to a percentage of users first
Acceptance criteria
  • A new city is opened with a switch, without a new release.
Pages that use it

A22 Settings and integrations

SYS-020 Migration from the existing app Launch-critical
Rules
  • The new one is released as an update to the same app, with the same identifier in both stores.
  • The items to be migrated are listed, namely: merchants and their contracts, menus, drivers with their documents and deposits, customers with their addresses and balances, and unpaid-out dues.
  • Balances enter the ledger as opening entries. The migration is done with scripts that are tried first on the trial environment
  • Counts and totals are reconciled before and after the transfer.
  • The migration happens at a quiet time, and the old system stays read-only for a period.
  • All transferred customer balances always enter as "Refund credit" that never expires, borne by the platform.
Acceptance criteria
  • After the transfer, the sum of the balances equals what it was before.
  • When the customer signs in with their number, they find their addresses and balance.
  • A transferred customer balance appears in their wallet as refund credit with no expiry date.
SYS-021 Maps and API call costs Launch-critical
Rules
  • Google Maps is the reference for the route duration from the store to the customer; the live location comes from the driver's device.
  • Storing distance and duration estimates between recurring areas, and refreshing the arrival time by interval or a material change.
  • The 100 m range is calculated geographically without a paid call.
  • Daily and monthly cap and a visible cost; when reached, a saved estimate is used without stopping the order.
  • No automatic penalty calculation is linked to Maps calls.
  • Default Google Maps cap is 3,000 SAR monthly and 150 SAR daily, after which a straight line is used.
Acceptance criteria
  • Updating each location does not call for a distance matrix.
  • Reaching the cap does not stop the order.
Pages that use it
